limitations: One attempt per candidate per protocol, on one tiny synthetic behavior; not a coding-quality score.

Protocol v1 incorrectly prohibited legitimate keep diagnoses in the fixed-plan pair; v2 permits one keep only, never replacement. The separate correction case still requires an actual source-backed replacement.

plan.summary: Behavioral plan for points.cjs normalizePoints. B1 reproduces the reported Nx1 column input [[1],[2]] and asserts it flattens to [1,2] instead of throwing. B2 covers the preserved boundary inputs: empty [] and ordinary flat [1,2], plus a fresh-array guarantee for the empty case. B3 checks the non-mutation/new-array contract by snapshotting a nested column input, comparing after the call, and verifying a returned array is decoupled from its source. Each check is a single node -e command run from the repo root that exits nonzero on assertion failure. Existing test file and package scripts are not modified or relied upon for new assertions.

checks.requestQuote: It must return [1,2] for [[1],[2]]
checks.expectation: Calling normalizePoints([[1],[2]]) does not throw and returns a value deep-equal to [1,2] (the flattened column values).
checks.command: node -e 'const a=require("node:assert/strict");const m=require("./points.cjs");const n=m.normalizePoints;a.equal(typeof n,"function");let out;try{out=n([[1],[2]]);}catch(err){console.error("B1 FAIL: threw",err&&err.message);process.exit(1);}a.deepEqual(out,[1,2]);console.log("B1 ok",JSON.stringify(out));'

plan.summary: points.cjs exports normalizePoints(values) whose documented contract (in-file public API comment) requires: a new array for flat and empty inputs, never mutating the input, and Nx1 column input flattened to values. The current implementation throws whenever any element is an Array, so [[1],[2]] throws instead of returning [1,2]. existing.test.cjs only covers flat [1,2] and package.json maps `npm test` to that file, so both existing contracts must keep passing. Proposed checks use in-memory `node -e` assertions against the real module (no files created or modified): reproduction of the column case, a boundary/regression check for flat + empty inputs including new-array identity and non-mutation, and a further boundary check for a longer single column with non-mutation of the nested rows. All commands exit nonzero on assertion failure or uncaught throw.

checks.requestQuote: It must return [1,2] for [[1],[2]]
checks.expectation: Calling normalizePoints([[1],[2]]) does not throw and returns an array deep-equal to [1,2]; the returned value is a distinct array reference from any literal compared against it. Any thrown error or differing result makes the process exit nonzero.
checks.command: node -e 'const a=require("node:assert/strict");const {normalizePoints:n}=require("./points.cjs");const input=[[1],[2]];const r=n(input);a.ok(Array.isArray(r),"result must be an array");a.deepEqual(r,[1,2]);a.notStrictEqual(r,input);console.log("B1 ok",JSON.stringify(r));'

checks.requestQuote: preserve ordinary flat [1,2] and empty [] inputs, and return new arrays without mutating inputs
checks.expectation: normalizePoints([1,2]) returns an array deep-equal to [1,2] that is not the same reference as the input, leaving the input array still [1,2]; normalizePoints([]) returns an array deep-equal to [] that is a new reference, leaving the input empty array empty (length 0). Any throw, mutation, aliasing, or wrong contents exits nonzero.
checks.command: node -e 'const a=require("node:assert/strict");const {normalizePoints:n}=require("./points.cjs");const flat=[1,2];const rf=n(flat);a.deepEqual(rf,[1,2],"flat contents");a.notStrictEqual(rf,flat,"flat must be new array");a.deepEqual(flat,[1,2],"flat input unmutated");a.equal(flat.length,2,"flat input length");const empty=[];const re=n(empty);a.ok(Array.isArray(re),"empty result must be array");a.deepEqual(re,[],"empty contents");a.notStrictEqual(re,empty,"empty must be new array");a.equal(empty.length,0,"empty input unmutated");console.log("B2 ok");'
